supplementaryNotes.text:
Learning notes: Learn Trading in Philippines

A localised free guide for Philippines learners — local regulator, local exchange, tax note and the same $100,000 virtual practice account.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Trading from Philippines

TradeHQ provides a free paper-trading environment for people in the Philippines who want to learn how US and global markets work without risking money. Real-money provider eligibility and rules should be checked against current official sources.

Publisher and source-check scope

Published by TradeHQ; site creator: Anuga Weerasinghe. Regulatory source check: 2026-10-18. Linked regulator or registry information; no verification of individual eligibility, tax rates or remittance permission. No professional legal or financial review.

Why practise first

Paper trading lets you learn market mechanics without opening or funding a real-money brokerage account. If you later consider real trading, verify the current requirements with the Philippine SEC, the exchange and the provider involved.

How market access works here

For real-money market access, check the Philippine SEC's current registry of capital-market participants and the provider's current terms. TradeHQ does not state that a particular bank setup, overseas platform, fractional product or account route is available to every resident. Nothing on TradeHQ requires a brokerage account or payment.

Regulation

For securities regulation and intermediary information, consult Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC Philippines). Registration for one activity does not establish that every product, overseas service or funding route is permitted. Use the official sources below for the applicable rules.

Broker types used locally
Broker/dealers and other capital-market participants listed in the Philippine SEC's current eRAMP registry
Starting capital and eligibility

TradeHQ does not publish a real-money starting amount because provider minimums, fees and personal circumstances vary. Use the simulator to learn the mechanics first, and verify any current account minimum or fee directly with a regulated provider.

Locally relevant assets to follow
The PSEi as the headline measure of local equity sentiment
USD/PHP, which matters to any household receiving remittances
The PSE’s dated index constituent and weight disclosures, rather than an assumed permanent sector ranking
US company reports as external research examples; virtual availability does not establish real-market access
Country-specific practice worksheet

Optional study worksheet: assume a fictional USD 100 remittance and choose two hypothetical PHP-per-USD rates. Calculate the peso receipt under each before fees. Then add an explicit fee assumption and compare the net receipts. This separates currency translation and transaction costs from an investment return. It does not forecast USD/PHP or establish a bank or brokerage route. Select a study schedule that fits school or work rather than following a foreign market overnight.

Tax

Tax treatment depends on current law, the product and individual circumstances. Check current official Philippine guidance or a qualified tax professional; TradeHQ does not provide tax advice. This is general information, not tax advice — confirm your own position with a qualified local professional.

If you are a student

Students and beginners can use the simulator and courses to practise market concepts and keep a record of simulated decisions without using real money.

Questions people in this country ask
Do I need to register with SEC Philippines to use TradeHQ? — TradeHQ is a free educational simulator with no real-money trades. For account eligibility or activities that require registration, check current Philippine SEC rules and the provider involved.
Can Filipino students under 18 use TradeHQ? — TradeHQ is a simulated educational site and does not execute real-money trades. Eligibility for a real brokerage account depends on the provider and applicable rules, so check current official/provider requirements rather than relying on this guide.
